title: Transformations of Quadratic Functions
seo_title: Algebra I Transformations of Quadratic Functions Worksheets (TEKS A.7C)
standard_text: A.7C determine the effects on the graph of the parent function f(x) = x^2 when f(x) is replaced by af(x), f(x) + d, f(x − c), f(bx) for specific values of a, b, c, and d
meta_desc: Free Algebra I worksheets for Texas TEKS A.7C: transformations of f(x) = x² — shifts, stretches, compressions and reflections, moving points and matching graphs. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Inside moves sideways (opposite sign); outside moves up or down.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The parent function is f(x) = x2, vertex (0, 0).
  • f(x) + d: up d. f(x − c): right c.
  • af(x): |a| > 1 is narrower, 0 < |a| < 1 is wider, a < 0 opens down.
  • f(bx) = (bx)2 = b2x2: |b| > 1 is narrower.

Examples

Example

g(x) = −2(x − 3)2 + 1

right 3, up 1

−2: narrower, opens down

Answer: vertex (3, 1), narrower, opens down

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Shifting left for (x − h)2Minus inside moves right.
Thinking 1/2 makes it narrowerA small |a| makes it wider.
Mixing up up and down+d outside moves up.

It flips the parabola to open down.

items.q: Describe how the graph of g(x) = (x + 2)² − 5 is related to the graph of the parent function f(x) = x².
items.e: Inside the function, (x + 2) moves the graph the opposite way: left 2. Outside, −5 moves it down. Shift left 2, down 5.
